findings.note: Ruling (A) — the 2026-08-29 owner ruling that a symlinked publication target is never read through, its PRE state is ABSENT, and the round-17 read-containment clause is retired in both directions — appears in this bundle only as the implementation report paraphrase and a code comment in _live_bytes. It is absent from investigation.md, where every other owner ruling in this package ((a), (b), (c), D(1)/D(2), E) is recorded with a verbatim dated quote; investigation.md carries no record of rounds 17-19 at all, and its newest per-document hash table still cites the ruling-(a)/(b)-era bytes (46d3143e...). The ruling is load-bearing: it authorizes a deviation from AC-047 and the Done When bullet, whose natural reading (every interrupted target byte-identical to its pre-invocation state) would preserve a symlinked entry, whereas under (A) a rollback restores ABSENT by unlinking, and the round-15 fixture assertion was rewritten to match; it also retired a security guard on a Security-Sensitive surface. From the bundle alone the authorization is self-attested and unverifiable. The code change itself is defensible and well tested (mutant K killed, three leaf-symlink assertions in both green-shipped captures); what is missing is the ruling record in the feature ruling ledger, the same amendment-propagation class this package has hit repeatedly, this time on the consent trail itself.

The WFI renumbering sentence is self-contradictory: renumbered from 038 ... main already carries a WFI-060. If main already carries WFI-060, renumbering TO 060 recreates the very collision the renumbering was for; the rationale only coheres if main carries WFI-038. One of the two numbers in the sentence is wrong, and as written a reader cannot tell whether the new number itself collides.
